lines: Settings now tunes how the 3D world is drawn, so the ride stays smooth on the device beside the bike.
Quality comes as five cards. Auto is chosen and recommended: it starts at Low and steps down whenever frames drop.
Pick a fixed level, and stepping down becomes yours to turn off. Frame rate, resolution and the graphics API sit below.
The world follows. A race opens at the level chosen, draws at most thirty frames a second when asked, and scales only its own pixels.
The World section, from a phone to the full screen.
Without WebGPU, Ultra waits for it. Without 3D at all, Settings says so, and every World control rests.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
